definition: One of two or more Lewis formulas for the same species that keep every atom in place but put the multiple bonds and lone pairs in different positions; the real species is a hybrid of them.
More than eight electrons in the valence shell of a central atom, as in $\ce{PCl5}$ or $\ce{SF6}$; only atoms in period 3 and below can have one.

The charge an atom would have if every bond were shared equally: valence electrons minus half the bonding electrons minus the non-bonding electrons; the preferred Lewis formula has formal charges closest to zero.
A compound containing a benzene ring, or a similar flat ring with a delocalized system of electrons, such as methylbenzene or phenol.
